question: The Soil Health Card Scheme mainly focuses on:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil nutrient assessment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Government of India in **February 2015** to promote sustainable farming by assessing soil health.
 
• The scheme primarily focuses on the **assessment of soil nutrients**, aiming to provide farmers with information on the nutrient status of their soil.
 
• The Soil Health Card includes details about **macro-nutrients (N, P, K), micro-nutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, etc.), and secondary nutrients (S, Mg, Ca)**, along with soil pH, organic carbon, and electrical conductivity.
 
• The purpose of the scheme is to enable farmers to **use fertilizers judiciously** and adopt appropriate soil management practices to enhance productivity.
 
• The Soil Health Card is issued every two years to farmers, helping them to monitor the health of their soil and take corrective actions accordingly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seed Certification**

 
 
• Seed certification is a quality assurance process for ensuring that seeds are of high quality, genetically pure, and free from diseases or pests.
 
• The process includes field inspections, testing, and labeling of seeds to meet prescribed standards.
 
• While it is a crucial agricultural practice, it is not directly related to soil health assessment.
 
 
 
• **Organic Inputs**
 
 
• Organic inputs refer to natural materials such as compost, manure, and bio-fertilizers used to enhance soil fertility and promote sustainable agriculture.
 
• Although organic inputs improve soil health, the Soil Health Card Scheme specifically focuses on the assessment of soil nutrients rather than the promotion of organic inputs.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms**
 
 
• Land reforms refer to changes in the ownership, operation, and distribution of land aimed at improving agricultural productivity and reducing rural poverty.
 
• Examples include land redistribution, consolidation of landholdings, and tenancy reforms.
 
• However, land reforms are not directly associated with the objectives of the Soil Health Card Scheme.
